channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Control electronics and cryogenics preset. Today's ranked reading list covers a scalable silicon spin-qubit architecture with logical operations (2611.33590), a 2D FPGA Union-Find decoder without global coordination (2611.33665), reproducible energy-relaxation distributions from broadband SWAP spectroscopy (2611.33854), high-throughput GPU decoding of quantum bivariate bicycle codes (2611.34481), and experimental quantum hardware benchmarks of flat non-Clifford hypergraph states on IBM Heron r2 (2611.34683), with the first three skimmed for transferable ideas and the latter two most directly informing HPC-assisted QEC and calibration-aware benchmarking for a small spin-qubit machine. No pay dirt today — 1 to skim.

item.title: Reproducible distributions of energy-relaxation times in superconducting qubits from broadband SWAP spectroscopy
item.description:
Skim new method — Cumulative distribution of qubit quality factor Q=2πf01T1 pooled over a 2.7 GHz SWAP spectroscopy sweep is repeatable with median Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance 0.03, within 1.4 times sampling floor, and reproducible across 4 thermal cycles spanning 326 days.

Grade 0.547 · 3.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Engineering the quantum-classical interface of solid-state qubits”

Figure

Quality factor spectra, CDFs, and percentile drift across 8 sweeps repeated every 9 hours over 3 days for zero bandwidth, 50 MHz bandwidth, and 2.7 GHz bandwidth. Only broadband sweeps achieve tightly overlapping CDFs and a median spread of 0.07 M (6%).

Asks

Can sweeping qubit frequency over a broad bandwidth yield an energy-relaxation metric whose distribution is stationary and reproducible in time?

Before

Repeated single-frequency T1 inversion recovery had median Q spread of 1.54 M (74%) and median Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance 0.57 over 3 days.

But

Fit quality threshold χr2<3 required. Reproducibility shifts when strongly coupled TLS defects reshuffle or leave sweep bandwidth after thermal cycling.

Tools

fast-flux-assisted (FFA) SWAP spectroscopy · aluminum-on-silicon flux-tunable transmon qubits · two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance · permutation test

Abstract

The distribution of the qubit energy-relaxation time (T1) in a superconducting quantum processor affects its logical error rates. However, reports on qubit fabrication quality focus on the median or best-case T1 from measurements that are not reproducible due to resonant coupling to two-level system (TLS) defects whose frequencies fluctuate in time. Here, we sweep the frequency f01 of a flux-tunable qubit over several GHz with SWAP spectroscopy, quoting the quality factor Q = 2 pi f01 T1 to make T1 comparable across frequencies. We show that the cumulative distribution of Q pooled over the sweep is reproducible across four thermal cycles spanning 326 days, up to the reshuffling of strongly coupled TLSs. In contrast to repeated measurements at a single frequency, the medians of the broadband Q distributions spread by an order of magnitude less over 3 days. The distance between the cumulative distributions of repeats comes close to its sampling floor only for the broadband sweeps. The broadband Q distribution further resolves small coherence differences between identically designed qubits on two dies of the same wafer. These results establish the broadband Q distribution as a reproducible metric for qubit fabrication quality.
